\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پرواز} (parvâz)}{پرواز (parvâz)}]{\fa{پرواز} (parvâz) — a flight}

\label{lesson:FA-C431-parvaz}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to be late, then the Persian for a loudspeaker.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پرواز}}
\textbf{\fa{پرواز}} (\emph{parvâz}) — \textquotedblleft{}a flight\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پرواز} \fa{ما} \fa{ساعت} \fa{شش} \fa{صبح} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Parvâz-e mâ sâ'at-e shesh-e sobh ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Our flight is at six in the morning.
\end{quote}

\emph{Parvâz-e mostaqim} — a direct flight.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{parvâz} is a native Persian word, which EtymDB lists with the sense 'flight'. It is usually linked with \emph{par} 'feather, wing', though EtymDB gives no older form.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{parvâz}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{parvâz}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{parvâz}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to be late, then the Persian for a loudspeaker, then say \emph{parvâz} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پرواز} \fa{کردن} (parvâz kardan)}{پرواز کردن (parvâz kardan)}]{\fa{پرواز} \fa{کردن} (parvâz kardan) — to fly}

\label{lesson:FA-C431-parvaz-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a loudspeaker, then the Persian for a flight.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پرواز} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{پرواز} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{parvâz kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to fly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{هواپیما} \fa{بالای} \fa{ابرها} \fa{پرواز} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Havâpeymâ bâlâ-ye abr-hâ parvâz mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The plane flies above the clouds.
\end{quote}

\emph{parvâz} + \emph{kardan}. Birds and planes both \emph{parvâz mikonand}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{parvâz kardan} is built from native \emph{parvâz} 'flight', which EtymDB lists, and \emph{kardan} 'to do', inherited from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{parvâz kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{parvâz kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a loudspeaker, then the Persian for a flight, then say \emph{parvâz kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{فرود} \fa{آمدن} (forud âmadan)}{فرود آمدن (forud âmadan)}]{\fa{فرود} \fa{آمدن} (forud âmadan) — to land (of a plane or a bird)}

\label{lesson:FA-C431-forud-amadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a flight, then the Persian for to fly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{فرود} \fa{آمدن}}
\textbf{\fa{فرود} \fa{آمدن}} (\emph{forud âmadan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to land (of a plane or a bird)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{هواپیما} \fa{در} \fa{باران} \fa{فرود} \fa{آمد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Havâpeymâ dar bârân forud âmad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The plane landed in the rain.
\end{quote}

\emph{forud} 'down' + \emph{âmadan} 'to come'. Present: \emph{forud miâyad}. Taking off is \emph{boland shodan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{forud âmadan} is built from native \emph{forud} 'down, below' and \emph{âmadan} 'to come', which EtymDB traces to the PIE root \emph{g\textsuperscript{w}em-} 'to step'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{forud âmadan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a flight, then the Persian for to fly, then say \emph{forud âmadan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{هواپیمایی} (havâpeymâyi)}{هواپیمایی (havâpeymâyi)}]{\fa{هواپیمایی} (havâpeymâyi) — an airline; aviation}

\label{lesson:FA-C431-havapeymayi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to fly, then the Persian for to land.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{هواپیمایی}}
\textbf{\fa{هواپیمایی}} (\emph{havâpeymâyi}) — \textquotedblleft{}an airline; aviation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{برادرم} \fa{در} \fa{یک} \fa{شرکت} \fa{هواپیمایی} \fa{کار} \fa{میکند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Barâdaram dar yek sherkat-e havâpeymâyi kâr mikonad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother works for an airline.
\end{quote}

Built on \emph{havâpeymâ} 'aeroplane' + \emph{-i}. An airline company is \emph{sherkat-e havâpeymâyi}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{havâpeymâyi} is built on \emph{havâpeymâ} 'aeroplane', from \emph{havâ} 'air', borrowed from Arabic \emph{hawāʾ} (EtymDB), and native \emph{peymâ} 'measuring, crossing', with the ending \emph{-i}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to fly, then the Persian for to land, then say \emph{havâpeymâyi} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کارت} \fa{پرواز} (kârt-e parvâz)}{کارت پرواز (kârt-e parvâz)}]{\fa{کارت} \fa{پرواز} (kârt-e parvâz) — a boarding pass, a boarding card}

\label{lesson:FA-C431-kart-e-parvaz}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to land, then the Persian for an airline.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کارت} \fa{پرواز}}
\textbf{\fa{کارت} \fa{پرواز}} (\emph{kârt-e parvâz}) — \textquotedblleft{}a boarding pass, a boarding card\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{کارت} \fa{پرواز} \fa{را} \fa{در} \fa{موبایلم} \fa{دارم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Kârt-e parvâz râ dar mobâylam dâram.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I have the boarding pass on my phone.
\end{quote}

\emph{kârt} 'card' + \emph{parvâz} 'flight'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kârt-e parvâz} is built from \emph{kârt} 'card', which EtymDB takes from French \emph{carte}, and native \emph{parvâz} 'flight'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
